hypothesis:
Take the throughput win that t0058 measured and threw away. That trial set torch.compile mode to 'max-autotune-no-cudagraphs' and reached 2921 steps against the champion's 2774 -- +5.3%, worth about -0.0029 bpb through the locally calibrated token law, larger than any single promotion in 428 trials. It recorded no metric because it ended as a TIMEOUT, and the distinction matters: the 300-second budget measures TRAINING, and compilation sits outside it, so a full backend search blows the process wall clock while the training window itself is untouched. The throughput was real. The harness discarded it for compile cost, and no trial revisited it in the 370 since.

The fix is to pay the search once instead of per trial. TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR pointed at a path shared across nodes lets the second and later runs reuse the autotuned configurations. I want to be explicit that this does not buy training time and is not a way of smuggling computation into the measured window: compilation is outside the 300s either way, so the cache changes only whether the process finishes inside the harness wall clock. If that reasoning is wrong the run will show it, because the training budget is enforced independently of anything I set here.

The companion trial 030 probes coordinate_descent_tuning, the cheap subset. This one probes the full mode. If both land, the difference tells me how much of the 5.3% needed a real backend search versus block-config tuning of kernels inductor already picked.
change_summary: Two edits. torch.compile(model, dynamic=False) gains mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs' -- no-cudagraphs specifically, because plain max-autotune has segfaulted through CUDA graphs on this kind of setup. And TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR is set via os.environ.setdefault before the torch import, pointing at a shared path outside the node tree, so the autotune search is amortised across trials. setdefault rather than assignment, so an externally supplied cache dir still wins. No change to the model, data, optimizer or training loop. The edit asserts no autotune mode and no cache dir are already set. Dry-run against champion source produced valid syntax at both sites.
expected_val_bpb_effect:
As with 030, the step count IS the mechanism here and I am registering that inversion in advance so it is not chosen after the fact. If steps land near t0058's 2921, the token law predicts -0.0029 and I expect the measured bpb to fall by roughly that; a large miss against that prediction falsifies the token law in this regime rather than the lever, which would be a more valuable finding than the promotion. If steps land near the champion's 2774, the cache did not help or the mode's gain does not reproduce on this device.
The outcome I am most alert to is a repeat timeout, producing no metric at all. If that happens the run still populates the shared cache, so the correct follow-up is the identical mode under a fresh source hash rather than abandoning the lever -- and I am stating that now because deciding it after a null would be reasoning backwards from the result.
risk:
A timeout burns this coordinate permanently, since known_hashes includes failures. I accept that because the payoff is several times a typical promotion and because a timed-out run still leaves the autotune cache warm for the retry, so the cost buys something even when it fails.
Three substantive risks. Autotuning is machine-state dependent: configurations are chosen against whatever SMs and clocks are free at compile time, and this is a shared box that has already produced a 23% slow device and power capping at 697 of 700W -- so a win here may not reproduce, and disagreement between the two confirmation runs would be signal rather than noise. A shared cache makes that worse, not better, because a configuration tuned under contention gets reused later under different conditions; if this becomes champion, that staleness is a standing liability worth revisiting rather than a solved problem. Finally, more steps means more passes over a fixed dataset, and this frame already sits near a two-epoch boundary, so a 5% step gain could partly trade throughput for overfitting -- which would show as bpb improving by materially less than the token law predicts.
